art.subject: Black Baza (Aviceda leuphotes), adult: head, long erect crest, neck, upperparts and tail glossy black; white and chestnut patches on the scapulars and secondaries; a broad white band across the upper breast below the black throat, bordered below by a black band; lower breast and belly buff with broad chestnut bars; vent and undertail coverts black. Bill short, dark grey, with two small tooth-like notches on the upper mandible; legs short, grey.
art.pose: perched upright on an exposed branch, side view, the long thin black crest standing up from the back of the head
art.scene: broadleaf woodland edge on a Korean offshore island during spring migration; no people, buildings or text
art.build: Small, crow-like raptor, a little larger than a feral pigeon, stocky, with a large head topped by a long, thin, erect crest. Bill short and hooked, much shorter than the head. Legs short. In flight broad, rounded, paddle-shaped wings, black above with white patches on the inner wing; from below black coverts and greyish flight feathers with black tips. Flies with crow-like flapping and short glides. Tail medium length, square and black.
avoid: Do not paint a short or missing crest; the black crest is long, thin and erect.
Do not paint it plain black like a crow or drongo; it has a white breast band and a chestnut-barred belly.
Do not give it long, pointed falcon wings; the wings are broad and rounded.
Do not paint a large eagle-like bill; the bill is short.
